justifications.functional_suitability: Real-Time Scoring Engine evaluates payments (R-01), Case Management Backend & UI with React Analyst Web App facilitates reviews (R-02), and Model & Rule Synchronizer enables zero-downtime model and rule updates using atomic references (R-03).
justifications.performance_efficiency: Real-Time Scoring Engine uses Go with in-process ONNX Runtime C-API, Feature Assembler queries Amazon ElastiCache Redis for sub-millisecond retrieval, and Audit Dispatcher offloads logs asynchronously to Audit Buffer Component (SQS), meeting the sub-50ms P99 target at 3,000 TPS.
justifications.compatibility: API Gateway accepts standard REST/HTTPS and gRPC from Merchant / Payment Gateway, while External Identity Provider integrates via standard OAuth2/OIDC protocols. Integration with external systems is clearly defined, with minor lack of schema specification.
justifications.usability: React Analyst Web App provides dedicated case workflows and WebSocket updates for Fraud Analysts and Risk Operations Managers. Query & Access Component (Amazon Athena) enables Compliance Auditors to query logs directly.
justifications.reliability: While Audit Buffer Component (SQS) decouples logging, the architecture lacks explicit fail-open mechanisms, circuit breakers, or fallback policies in API Gateway and Real-Time Scoring Engine to prevent blocking payments for over one minute during scoring outages (R-07).
justifications.security: AWS WAF, External IdP MFA, Tamper-Evident Vault Component (S3 Object Lock), and data masking in FastAPI Case Management Backend provide strong protection, though a dedicated tokenization service or AWS KMS mechanism for card encryption is omitted.
justifications.maintainability: Clear separation of concerns across Real-Time Scoring Engine, Case Management Backend & UI, and Feature Store. Using managed services like AWS ECS Fargate, Lambda, and Athena minimizes operational overhead for a three-engineer team.
justifications.portability: Containers run on AWS ECS Fargate in eu-west-1 as requested. While heavily coupled to proprietary AWS services like S3 Object Lock, SQS, and Athena, it adapts effectively to the specified target cloud environment.

PERF-01.justification: The scoring engine utilizes compiled in-process ONNX C-API inference, sub-millisecond ElastiCache Redis lookups, and asynchronous audit dispatching to easily achieve sub-50 ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS.
sensitivity_points: Network latency and serialization overhead between the scoring engine and ElastiCache Redis
tradeoffs: Asynchronous audit logging sacrifices immediate persistence consistency to guarantee sub-50 ms P99 response

PERF-02.justification: Case management runs in an isolated container on Fargate, preventing resource contention with scoring. However, the architecture lacks a case database or queue connecting scoring to case management.
sensitivity_points: Resource isolation between operational analytical queries and scoring feature stores
tradeoffs: Separating case management onto independent infrastructure increases deployment complexity but prevents scoring degradation

AVAIL-01.justification: The architecture does not define a fallback path, circuit breaker, or default-allow mechanism in the API Gateway or Scoring Engine if scoring services fail or crash.
sensitivity_points: Health check intervals and failover routing logic configured in API Gateway
tradeoffs: Static fallback routing preserves payment flow availability at the risk of accepting fraudulent transactions

AVAIL-02.justification: Scoring uses an asynchronous Audit Dispatcher and Audit Log Storage includes an Amazon SQS buffer to decouple scoring latency from downstream S3 or ingestion slowdowns.
sensitivity_points: In-memory buffer capacity of the Audit Dispatcher and SQS retention during prolonged outages
tradeoffs: Queue-based buffering prevents request blocking but delays audit log finality in Object Lock storage

MOD-01.justification: The Model & Rule Synchronizer uses an atomic in-memory swap (atomic.Value) in Go to deploy new ONNX models loaded from S3 without service interruption or downtime.
sensitivity_points: Memory overhead of holding two ONNX model runtime instances during atomic swap
tradeoffs: Local container model caching avoids external network hops at the cost of transient memory duplication

MOD-02.justification: In-memory rule synchronization allows atomic rule reloading, but the architecture lacks an authoring/publishing workflow and velocity feature calculation pipelines needed for new analyst rules.
sensitivity_points: Frequency and propagation latency of rule synchronization polling across distributed engine tasks
tradeoffs: Dynamic rule swapping avoids rebuilds but requires strict schema validation to prevent runtime panics

SEC-01.justification: Data masking and RBAC are provided in the case management backend, but the architecture lacks automated anomaly detection or alerting mechanisms to identify compromised accounts within 15 minutes.
sensitivity_points: Enforcement of field-level tokenization and masking in the backend API layer
tradeoffs: Masking card details preserves PCI compliance but limits analyst visibility during forensic investigation

SEC-02.justification: Audit Log Storage natively enforces 7-year WORM compliance via S3 Object Lock, while serverless Amazon Athena querying enables retrieval and reproduction of past decisions within hours.
sensitivity_points: Partitioning strategy of S3 audit objects for cost and query execution efficiency in Athena
tradeoffs: Storing full decision inputs and explanations in S3 increases storage cost but guarantees explainability
